title: Isothermal compression of a Fermi gas to deep quantum degeneracy
authors: Kirill Karpov, Jonas Auch, Eduard Heidt, Florian Kiesel, Alexandre De Martino, Christian Groß
abstract: The standard approach for generating deeply degenerate quantum gases is evaporative or sympathetic cooling in a harmonic trap, after which the gas has reached its minimum entropy. All subsequent state transformations rely on adiabatic changes of a closed system, and coupling to the environment or non-adiabatic processes monotonically increase the entropy. Here, we demonstrate that this experimental paradigm can be bypassed by utilizing species-selective trapping with a low-dissipation optical tune-out trap in a dual-species mixture. We successfully reduce the entropy of a two-component fermionic quantum gas via isothermal compression within a bosonic bath, reaching deep quantum degeneracy of $T/T_F = 0.024^{+0.007}$, with $T_F$ the Fermi temperature. By characterizing the cross-dimensional relaxation and thermalization, we demonstrate that cooling light fermions with heavy bosons remains efficient and fast, even deep in the degenerate regime, where the thermalization time is found to be independent of $T/T_F$. Our results pave the way for direct cooling within optical lattices, box traps, or other complex potentials, thereby eliminating the reliance on adiabatic state transformations to reach strongly interacting many-body regimes.
summary: The research overcomes the fundamental entropy limitations of traditional evaporative cooling in ultracold atomic gases. By implementing isothermal compression using a bosonic bath to cool fermionic atoms, the authors achieved deep quantum degeneracy. This method paves the way for direct state preparation in complex traps without relying on slow adiabatic ramps.
main_problem: The standard adiabatic cooling methods limit the entropy available for reaching deeply degenerate quantum gas states.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated that isothermal compression, achieved via a bosonic bath, can bypass entropy limitations to reach deep degeneracy ($T/T_F = 0.024$).
method: They utilized species-selective trapping with an optical tune-out beam in a dual-species mixture ($	ext{Er}/	ext{Li}$) to maintain constant temperature during compression.
model_or_system: The system is a two-component fermionic quantum gas (Li) cooled by coupling it to a bosonic bath ($	ext{Er}$) within an optical trap setup. The process involves isothermal compression, which maintains $T$ while decreasing entropy via the bath interaction.
key_observables: Reduced temperature ($T/T_F$), entropy per particle ($S/N$), and interspecies thermalization time ($	au_{	ext{thermal}}$).
important_parameters: $T/T_F = 0.024^{+0.007}$; the thermalization time is found to be independent of $T/T_F$.
main_assumptions: Sympathetic thermometry using the bosonic component ($	ext{Er}$) is necessary for accurate low-$T/T_F$ measurements due to noise broadening.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup, dual-species evaporation trajectories, and time evolution of temperature and atom number during compression protocols.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem with adiabatic cooling limitations. It then details the isothermal compression protocol using a bosonic bath to bypass entropy constraints. Finally, it characterizes the efficiency and speed of thermalization in this deep degenerate regime.
why_interesting: This work provides an alternative pathway for reaching strongly interacting many-body regimes by replacing slow, entropy-limited adiabatic cooling with fast, controlled isothermal processes, which is highly relevant for quantum simulation.
